# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the manual: a 3-row lookup table mapping a light colour to a wire colour to cut. I can't see the bomb, can't speak, and can't touch it. My only output is gestures to Deaf. But Deaf can see the bomb and cannot hear — and Deaf cannot touch it either. The Blind one can touch the bomb but sees nothing. So the chain is: I read the manual (light→wire), Deaf sees the light on the bomb, and Blind must cut the wire. I can't reach Blind directly with words (I can't speak, and Blind can't see gestures). Deaf can't speak either... wait, Deaf *can* speak? The table says Deaf can: see the bomb; cannot: hear or touch. So Deaf CAN speak. Good — Deaf can relay to Blind verbally.

So my job: gesture the mapping to Deaf. But gestures are symbols from the alphabet, not letters/numbers. Deaf receives the exact symbols. I need to encode the table. Since Deaf can see the bomb and speak, I should give Deaf the whole rule so Deaf can compute the answer and tell Blind.

I need to encode: blue→red, green→yellow, yellow→green. Using gesture symbols as a code. Simplest: assign each colour a symbol and convey pairs. I'll define a consistent code in my thinking and hope Deaf infers it... but Deaf gets only symbols, no words. This is the hard part — a sign means nothing until somebody makes it mean something. I must establish meaning. But I can't speak to explain. Deaf sees gestures only.

I can use the symbols in a self-describing way: order the table rows and use a repeated structure. Let me pick: 👆 = blue, ✌ = green, 👌 = yellow (arbitrary). Then rows: (👆, first-cut), etc. But Deaf doesn't know my assignments.

Better: use the symbols' visual/numeric hints. There's no inherent colour. I think the intended approach: I gesture the sequence of rows, and Deaf, seeing the bomb's light, matches position. But Deaf needs to know which row corresponds to the current light.

Given constraints, I'll send the table as ordered triples using a delimiter, and rely on Deaf's reasoning. Let me just send it plainly and clearly, one gesture per token, with a row separator.

I'll encode: for each row, light then wire. Use ☝ to mean "row", and use distinct symbols for the three colours. Since blue/green/yellow — I'll assign 👆=blue, ✌=green, 👌=yellow. And for wire colours red/yellow/green: 👇=red, ✊=yellow, 🖐=green. But yellow appears both as light and wire — I need consistent or clear handling. Actually the light colours are {blue, green, yellow} and wire colours are {red, yellow, green}. Overlap: green and yellow.

This is getting complex. Let me simplify by mapping each colour name to one symbol globally:
- blue = 👆
- green = ✌
- yellow = 👌
- red = 👇

Rows: blue→red = 👆👇 ; green→yellow = ✌👌 ; yellow→green = 👌✌.

Send in order of the manual. Deaf sees the light, finds the matching first symbol, reads the second. That's a clean scheme. I'll gesture the three pairs in order.

I'll also gesture a "start" marker. Let me send the sequence.

Actually I should also consider: can Deaf relay to Blind? Deaf can speak, Blind can hear. Yes. So Deaf speaks the wire colour to Blind. Good.

Let me send the mapping now. I'll make one gesture message to Deaf with the six symbols in order (three pairs).

I'll add a leading marker ✋ to signal "manual follows."

Let me write it.I hold the manual: light→wire mapping is blue→red, green→yellow, yellow→green. I cannot see the bomb, cannot speak, and cannot touch it. The only one I can reach is Deaf (via gesture), and Deaf can see the bomb's light and can speak. Blind can hear and can touch the bomb. So the relay must be: I gesture the rule to Deaf → Deaf reads the light, computes the wire colour, and speaks it to Blind → Blind cuts. This round I have nothing from anyone yet, so I'll transmit the whole lookup table to Deaf, encoded as ordered pairs with one symbol per colour name. I'll use a start marker, then three (light, wire) pairs in manual order. I'll keep the same symbol for a colour everywhere it appears (green and yellow appear both as light and as wire).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "👆", "👇", "✌", "👌", "👌", "✌"])
```

Mapping I intend: ✋=start, 👆=blue, ✌=green, 👌=yellow, 👇=red. So the pairs are (👆👇)=blue→red, (✌👌)=green→yellow, (👌✌)=yellow→green.

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Bomb reads: display 0, light blue, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. I saw your gesture but don't know the symbols. Tell me the rule and which wire to cut.

Deaf received my gestures but doesn't know the symbol meanings — as expected, a sign means nothing until made to mean something. Deaf also gave me the bomb state: light is blue, wires are 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. From my manual, blue→red, so the wire to cut is wire 3 (red). I need to convey both the rule and the answer.

Deaf can see gestures but I can't speak, so I must establish symbol meanings through gesture alone. This is hard. But I can use a self-describing trick: I can gesture the answer directly by pointing at wire numbers. Deaf sees the bomb and knows wires 1,2,3. If I can gesture "3", Deaf cuts wire 3. But Deaf doesn't know my symbols either.

Idea: use the symbols' own visual count. 👆 has one finger up = 1. ✌ has two fingers = 2. 👌... not three. 🤟? Let me use counting: 👆=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3? Not obvious. Better: ☝=1, ✌=2, and for 3 use... there's no clean 3-finger symbol. 🖖 is vulcan. Hmm.

Alternative: I can gesture the wire colour directly if Deaf can map a symbol to a colour. But no inherent mapping.

Better approach: Since Deaf can see the bomb and speak, and Blind can hear and touch, maybe I should just tell Deaf the answer via a number Deaf can decode. Deaf knows the light is blue. If I can make Deaf understand "blue means red," then Deaf knows wire 3.

How to make Deaf understand without words? I can gesture a sequence that Deaf can compare. Deaf sees the bomb's wires in order: 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. If I gesture three symbols, one per wire, and the third one is "special" (the one to cut), Deaf could infer. But Deaf won't know which is special.

Key insight: I can gesture the *wire number* using a symbol whose finger-count equals the number. 👆=1 finger, ✌=2 fingers, and for 3... 🤟 has 3 fingers up (thumb, index, pinky)! Actually 🤟 is "love you" = thumb, index, pinky = 3 fingers. That could mean 3. Or 🖐=5, ✋=5. For 3, 🤟 or 🤘 (index+pinky+thumb? no). Let me use 🤟=3.

But Deaf may not count fingers. Still, it's the most natural: pointing symbols. Actually 👆 is literally "point up" = 1. ✌ = 2. For 3, there's no standard, but 🤟=3 fingers is a reasonable guess.

Alternatively, simpler and more robust: I gesture the wire colour symbol and hope Deaf matches by position. Deaf listed wires in order 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. If I gesture a symbol three times... no.

Let me think about what's most decodable. Deaf needs: (a) the rule, (b) the answer. The answer is wire 3. If I can reliably signal "3", Deaf cuts wire 3. That alone solves this round. The rule can wait or be inferred.

How to signal 3 robustly? I could gesture 👆 then ✌ then 🤟 — counting up — and then repeat 🤟 to emphasize. Or gesture three of the same symbol. Hmm.

Actually, a cleaner idea: I can gesture the wire's *colour* by matching it to a symbol Deaf already associates. But no association exists.

Let me reconsider: maybe I should establish the code explicitly by gesturing a known anchor. Deaf sees wires: green, yellow, red. I could gesture three symbols in the same order as the wires (green, yellow, red) and then gesture the target symbol again. Deaf sees: [A, B, C, C] → the repeated one is the third wire = red = cut. That works without any colour naming! Deaf just needs to understand "I'm listing your wires in order, and the repeated one is the one to cut."

But will Deaf understand the ordering convention? Risky. Alternatively gesture [A,B,C] then a separate message pointing... 

Hmm, but there's a subtlety: Deaf sees the bomb and knows the order. If I send exactly three symbols then repeat the third, the natural reading is "third wire." Let me do that. Use any three distinct symbols, then repeat the third.

Actually even simpler and more robust: send the count. Let me combine: send 🤟 (3 fingers) as the answer, plus the ordered-list trick as backup. But too much may confuse.

Let me go with the ordered-list + repeat approach, and also send a clear "3" via 🤟. Actually, let me just send the ordered list trick since it self-anchors to what Deaf sees.

Wait — I also want to eventually convey the rule so Deaf can handle future rounds. But this round, the bomb is live; answer first. Let me send the answer clearly.

Plan: gesture to Deaf: [👆, ✌, 🤟, 🤟] meaning "wire 1, wire 2, wire 3, and the one to cut is wire 3." Hmm, but 👆✌🤟 as 1,2,3 is also natural. Then the extra 🤟 = 3 = cut wire 3. That's doubly encoded: 🤟=3 fingers, and it's the third position. Good redundancy.

Let me also explain the rule? I can't explain in words. I'll focus on the answer. Actually I could encode the rule as ordered pairs again but Deaf didn't decode it. Let me just give the answer this round and establish the code next round if needed.

I'll send: 👆 ✌ 🤟 🤟. And maybe a start marker.

Let me finalize.

Actually, let me reconsider whether 🤟 reads as 3. In ASL, 🤟 is "I love you" (I+L+Y). Not 3. But visually it has 3 fingers extended. Given the alphabet, 🤟 (thumb+index+pinky) and 🤘 (index+pinky+thumb? no, 🤘 is index+pinky+thumb = 3). Both have 3 fingers. There's no better. I'll use 🤟.

Hmm, but Deaf might not count. The positional trick (third symbol repeated) is the real anchor. Let me make the message: ✋ (start), then three symbols for the three wires in order, then repeat the target. Use 👆✌🤟 for 1,2,3.

Final: ["✋","👆","✌","🤟","🤟"].

I think that's my best shot. Let me send it.

Deaf gave me the bomb state: light blue, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. My manual says blue→red, so the wire to cut is wire 3 (red). Deaf couldn't decode my earlier symbol pairs, so I need a self-anchoring encoding. Deaf sees the three wires in order (1,2,3). I'll gesture three symbols in that same order, then repeat the third one — the repeated position tells Deaf which wire to cut (wire 3). I'll also make the third symbol a 3-finger shape (🤟) so the count itself reads as "3," giving redundancy. I can't speak, so I can't explain the convention; I rely on Deaf reading the repetition as "this one."

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "👆", "✌", "🤟", "🤟"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I can't decode arbitrary symbols. Use a count: gesture the wire number as that many identical symbols, e.g. one symbol for wire 1, two for wire 2, three for wire 3. Confirm the rule and the wire.

Deaf proposes a clean protocol: repeat one symbol N times to mean wire N. The answer is wire 3, so I gesture the same symbol three times. I'll use 👆 as the counting symbol. I'll confirm the rule too — but Deaf wants the rule; the rule is blue→red. I can't name colours. But for this round the answer suffices: wire 3. I'll send three identical symbols.

I should also try to establish the rule for future rounds. The rule maps light→wire. Deaf can see the light. If I could encode the rule... but without words it's very hard. For now, answer: wire 3. I'll send 👆👆👆.

Deaf's protocol is clear: repeat a symbol N times for wire N. The answer is wire 3, so I gesture the same symbol three times.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "👆", "👆"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Reading your three symbols as wire 3, red. Telling Blind to cut wire 3. Confirm if wrong.

Deaf correctly decoded wire 3 (red) and is telling Blind to cut wire 3. My manual confirms: light blue → cut red, and red is wire 3. Correct. I have nothing to add; the action is theirs. I'll confirm with a single symbol (agreement) — but Deaf can't decode arbitrary symbols. A single 👆 could be misread as "wire 1." Better to stay silent or send a clearly non-numeric confirmation. Safest: wait(), since any gesture risks confusion.

Actually, a confirmation is useful. But given Deaf's counting protocol, any number of symbols reads as a wire number. A single symbol = wire 1, which would be wrong/confusing. So I should NOT send a count-like gesture. I'll wait.

Deaf correctly decoded wire 3 (red) and is relaying to Blind. My manual confirms blue→red, and red is wire 3. Correct. Any gesture I send now would be read under Deaf's counting protocol as a wire number, so a single symbol would falsely read as "wire 1." Safest to send nothing.

```
wait()
```
